title: Aniimo Homeland Guide | Work Abilities, Best Workers, Personalities And RV Levels | Aniimo Guide
description: A full guide to working your Aniimo Homeland: how to unlock it, how RV levels raise your worker cap, all thirteen work abilities, the best early and long term workers, personality bonuses, food and temperature. Checked against several guides in October 2026.

sections.heading: Your Homeland needs a plan
sections.script: If you reached level twenty in Aniimo and opened the RV, you now have a Homeland, and a lot of players treat it as a place to dump creatures and forget about it. That is a mistake. A well run Homeland makes food, materials, Aniipods and eggs while you explore, and the secret is putting the right Aniimo in the right job. In this video we explain the thirteen work abilities, which facilities they run, the best workers to use early and for the long term, how personalities give a twenty percent bonus, how RV levels open more space, and how to keep your workers fed. We will not repeat our breeding and egg video, so this one is only about the work. As always, patches can change numbers, so trust your own game screen first.

sections.heading: Getting into the Homeland
sections.script: Guides say the Homeland opens once you reach character level twenty. You start the quest called Prologue: The Wondrous RV from the Quests tab, and an inventor named Fannie hands over your first RV. Think of the RV level as the main progress bar of your whole base. Every level adds more room, more facilities and better rewards. The Production Zone has sixteen plots, and each plot needs an RV level at least equal to its number before you can buy it. Clearing debris on a new plot also gives Wood Blocks and Mineral Sand, which help with upgrades. One tip from a playthrough guide is that there is no advantage to buying plots early, so buy them when you actually need the space and leave room for later facilities.

sections.heading: How RV levels open more workers
sections.script: The most useful thing an RV level does is raise the number of Aniimo you can place at home. At RV level two you can place eight Aniimo, and Storage Units unlock, which lets Hauling workers carry goods to your warehouse. Level three raises the cap to eleven, level four to fourteen, level five to seventeen, and level six to twenty. Two more details matter. At level four you can refresh your orders, and at level six you get the Signal Transmitter, so Aniimo can go on trips and bring back items and Mysterious Aniimo Eggs. Level eight opens the Homebuilding Zone, a separate area for your own house and decorations. It shares the same Aniimo limit as the production area, so every worker you put there is a slot you cannot use elsewhere.

sections.heading: The thirteen work abilities
sections.script: Now the core system. Aniimo do not work with their combat stats. They work with Homeland abilities, and the database lists thirteen of them. Hauling, Leisure, Artisanship, Perfumery, and then the nine elements Grass, Wind, Fire, Water, Earth, Dark, Lightning, Ice and Light. Each ability has a level, and a higher level means faster work. The element abilities cover the farm and the kitchen. Grass plants seeds and gathers, Water brews and fetches water, Fire cooks and smelts, Earth cultivates land and mines, Dark harvests, cuts, pickles and dries, and Wind processes products. Lightning handles machines like the Aniipod Maker, Ice runs the Cooling Unit, and Light runs the Sunlamp. Hauling moves goods, Artisanship crafts, Leisure runs the relaxing facilities, and Perfumery is a special job for making perfume.

sections.heading: Match the worker to the facility
sections.script: A good habit is to start from the facility and work backward. A guide lists which ability each facility asks for. Farmland and Woodland use Grass, Water, Dark and Earth. The Mine uses Earth. The Blazing Stove, Chimney Kiln, Claw Game Cooker and Simmering Pot use Fire. The Carousel Mill and Joy Wheel Loom use Wind. The Crafting Table and Woodworking Bench use Artisanship. The Nimbus Bed, Dewy House and Starfall Hammock use Leisure, and the Phonolfactory Table uses Perfumery. In your Aniimo management screen there is an exclamation mark next to ability distribution, and Game8 says it estimates how many of each ability your Homeland needs. Use it. It is much better to cover the abilities you need than to try to cover every element.

sections.heading: Best early workers
sections.script: You will already own several good beginners by the time the Homeland opens. Budclaw has Grass, Earth and Hauling at level one, so it can clear land, sow and store goods. Dewy has Dark, Leisure and Perfumery at level one and its perfume skill is needed for the Dewy House. Skippy has Water and Hauling at level one, and watering crops shortens their growth time. Flutternym has Wind and Leisure at level one and can run the Carousel Mill. These are fine for starting, but every one of their abilities is only level one, so think of them as temporary. The good news is that evolution helps a lot. Budclaw evolves into Shrubclaw, and Shrubclaw jumps to Earth level three and Hauling level three, which makes it a strong early miner.

sections.heading: Best long term workers
sections.script: For the long run, look for level three abilities. Scorchhowl has Fire three and Hauling three, so it can cook, smelt and carry. Stellarys has Dark three and Leisure three. Turbo has Wind three and Leisure three, a direct upgrade over Flutternym. Glynsera has Ice three and Hauling three, which is perfect for the Cooling Unit. Blazen has Lightning three and Artisanship three, so it makes Aniipods quickly and also helps at the Crafting Table. Leafy has Grass three, Water two and Hauling three, a great all rounder for the farm. Glacy has Water three, and it is very good at fetching water from the Well. The best ones overall are Somniwing and Irisalis, which both have Grass four and Leisure four. Because slots are limited, prefer creatures with several high abilities.

sections.heading: Personalities give a twenty percent bonus
sections.script: Every Aniimo has a four letter personality like ESTJ, and it matters at home as well as in battle. Each letter gives a twenty percent work bonus, but only at certain facilities. Energetic works best at the Bouncy Brew Keg and Woodworking Bench. Instinctive likes the Phonolfactory Table and Dewy House. Practical is good at the Claw Game Cooker and Chimney Kiln. Nimble boosts the Jukebox Dryer, Blazing Stove and Floral Windmill. Tenacious boosts the Carousel Mill and Simmering Pot. Faithful boosts the Joy Wheel Loom, Well and Starfall Hammock. Judicious helps the Crafting Table, Tidewhisper Sandcastle and Nimbus Bed, and Playful helps the Mine and Pickling Jar. So one Aniimo can get four facility bonuses at once. Check the ability first, then use personality as the tie breaker.

sections.heading: Food, temperature and light
sections.script: Workers need food, and both Game8 and the database agree on the numbers. Energy Bites give one thousand food, Wheatmeal gives nine thousand three hundred seventy, and Bread gives twenty six thousand seven hundred forty. Wheatmeal comes from grinding wheat, so it is a great cheap start, and Bread is the better upgrade later. If your food runs dry, work slows down and workers can get sick. Visit your Homeland at least once a day to look after them. Temperature is the other puzzle. Some crops need a Cool, Warm, Freezing or Scorching area, and the Heat Furnace and Cooling Unit create those zones. Their ranges can overlap. Set the Cooling Unit to Freeze and the Heat Furnace to Warm, and the area between becomes Cool. Sunlamps need a Light Aniimo, and Lunara and Helion both have it.

sections.heading: Which job is your best worker doing
sections.script: That is our guide to Aniimo Homeland work. Remember the main points. Pick workers by their ability level, not their combat level. Evolve them, because evolved forms usually have higher abilities. Match personalities to facilities for the extra twenty percent. Keep your food stocked, and use your limited slots on creatures with several strong abilities. Now we want to hear from you. Which Aniimo is your best Homeland worker, and what is the first facility you build? Tell us in the comments.
